Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
I am not sure of my "Crusade Ratio" yet, but I can say that for the first
time ever I got 2 copies of the same vampire in one booster. (Shahid)

What are the odds of that? (Should it be possible with the way boosters are
randomized at all?)

Messages.Author: John P.
Messages.Body:
"Jozxyqk" <jfeu...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote in message news:5f7rc.39332$6f5.4134210@attbi_s54...


Assuming the vampires are random in each booster:

Chance of no Shahid:
(49/50)*(49/50)*(49/50)=94.1%

Chance of 1 Shahid:
(1/50)*(49/50)*(49/50)*3 = 5.76%

Chance of 2 Shahid:
(1/50)*(1/50)*(49/50) *3 = 0.12 %

Chance of 3 Shahid:
(1/50)*(1/50)*(1/50) = 1/125,000 or really really small

If we ignore the fact that it is Shahid the chance
of getting two of the same vampire is

Chance of getting 2 Shahid * 50 (50 different vampires) = 5.8%

-JTP

Look at it this way. If the odds are actually 5.8% if the
vampires are truely random (more than 1 in 20) then we
would probably see 1 or two boosters like this in
every box. As we do not see it that often, its likely that
there is a mechanism to prevent this, and the pack you got
is a freak accident.

So while it may have seemed rhetorical, there was actually
a valuable answer buried in there. :D
Besides, I'm bored.

-JTP
